display.title: Why Is It Called Rosh Hashanah? The Head of the Year
display.summary_short: Why Rosh Hashanah is the 'head' of the year and not just its beginning, from the Mitteler Rebbe's Ateres Rosh, and how Selichos prepare us for it.
display.summary_long: A short pre-Rosh Hashanah talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi asks why the holiday is called Rosh Hashanah, the head of the year, and not Techilas Hashanah, the beginning of the year. The answer comes from Ateres Rosh, 'the crown of the head', a sefer by the Mitteler Rebbe, the son of the Alter Rebbe. Just as the head is the most important part of the body and the source of life and strength for every limb, Rosh Hashanah gives life to every day of the coming year, and all of the year's blessings are sent on these two days. So we must be very careful how we behave, daven and do mitzvos on Rosh Hashanah, because it leaves its mark on the whole year. He then explains Selichos, the prayers for forgiveness said every morning that week, with resolutions such as more respect for parents and better behavior in school, so that Hashem, like a king in the field, will grant a good and sweet year.
display.lesson: Rosh Hashanah is the head of the whole year: how we act and daven on it shapes every day that follows.
